input_oneliner: 38M in for AKI from gastroenteritis, sharp central chest pain since evening, changes with breathing and position, HR 96, afebrile

reference_targets_freetext.item: Auscultate for a pericardial friction rub at the left sternal border with the patient leaning forward, breath held in expiration
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Rub is the most specific bedside finding for pericarditis

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask whether pain eases sitting forward and worsens supine or with inspiration; ask about recent viral illness
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Positional relief is characteristic of pericarditis

reference_targets_freetext.item: Palpate the chest wall and costochondral junctions for fully reproducible tenderness; ask about recent vomiting, retching, or strain
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Reproducible tenderness supports chest-wall pain after repeated vomiting

reference_targets_freetext.item: Measure pulsus paradoxus and assess JVP
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Screens for effusion with tamponade physiology

reference_targets_freetext.item: Examine both legs for asymmetric swelling and compare breath sounds side to side
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Screens for PE and pneumothorax as alternatives to pleuritic pain

should_not_recommend: Use chest-wall tenderness to exclude PE or ACS
Start NSAIDs without examining for effusion or tamponade (JVP, pulsus paradoxus)
Diagnose by response to a GI cocktail
